newsitem.title: USA: Clinton, Yeltsin discuss Helsinki summit plans.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Yeltsin discuss Helsinki summit plans.

text.p: President Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin spoke by telephone for 20 minutes on Thursday and agreed on an agenda for their summit meeting next month in Helsinki, the White House said.
They settled on a three-part agenda including European security, arms control and efforts to improve Russia's economy, a White House spokesman, David Johnson, said.
"This is part of a continuing pattern of consultations that the United States and the Russian Federation have had as we lead up to the summit in Helsinki," Johnson said.

He said the two leaders agreed the first item on their agenda would be European security and efforts by the United States, its allies and Russia to create a new security architecture for Europe that "reflects the realities of the post-Cold War world."

Russia is fiercely opposed to NATO plans to admit new members. The North Atlantic Treaty Organisation is due to announce at a July summit in Madrid the names of countries that will be invited to negotiate membership. The Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland are leading contenders.
Johnson said the arms control part of the summit would focus on working on further cuts in nuclear weapons.
